base_member_text: [L63-L70,L132-L137,L197-L207,L267-L276] (MED/saved-workspace shape) All saved allocatable workspaces are sized only on their first call and never checked against the current grid dimensions, so reuse after a grid-size change is unsafe.
audit_member_text: [L63-L70,L132-L137,L197-L207,L267-L276] (LOW/state/dimension lifecycle) Saved scratch arrays in all formulations are allocated only once and never resized, so reuse with a different grid shape has stale bounds.

base_member_text: [L105-L111,L173-L179] (HIGH/dry-depth division) ROELVINK2 and ROELVINK_DALY multiply dissipation by H/hh without a local wet mask or positive hh guard.
audit_member_text: [L99-L111,L167-L179] (HIGH/dry-cell division) BREAK_ROELVINK2 and Daly scale dissipation by H/hh without a wet mask or positive-depth guard.

base_member_text: [L77-L84,L143-L150] (HIGH/dry-depth division) The non-Daly Roelvink formulas divide by hhw over complete rows or full arrays before restricting the result to an active region, with no wet mask or positive-depth floor in this routine.
audit_member_text: [L77-L84,L143-L150] (HIGH/dry-cell invalid arithmetic) Roelvink breaking computes H divided by depth-dependent limits over unmasked arrays, so zero-depth cells can evaluate 0/0 and contaminate Qb.

base_member_text: [L86-L97,L151-L165] (MED/stale state) The Daly branch deliberately retains Qb inside the hysteresis band but also leaves dry-cell Qb unchanged, after which dissipation is recomputed from that potentially stale value.
audit_member_text: [L86-L97,L151-L165] (MED/stale dry-cell output) The Daly branch updates Qb only at wet cells but then computes D for the full addressed row/domain, leaving dry-cell Qb and potentially D dependent on prior state.

base_member_text: [L282-L298] (HIGH/unchecked singular denominator) The Janssen-Battjes implementation divides by raw k when forming Hb and by raw hh when forming D, unlike the neighboring Baldock implementation's k floor.
audit_member_text: [L282-L298] (HIGH/unchecked wave-number/depth denominator) Janssen-Battjes divides directly by k when forming Hb and by hh when forming D, unlike the guarded k division in Baldock, so calm or dry points can generate infinities/NaNs.

base_member_text: [L211-L231] (LOW/parameter-domain contract) The Baldock calculation floors k only in the Hb denominator while kh and the spatial gamma use the raw k, leaving negative or otherwise invalid wave-number inputs inconsistently treated.

[L79-L84,L145-L150] (MED/real-power domain) The breaking argument raises an unconstrained H-to-depth ratio to the real-valued parameter n, so a negative ratio with non-integer n would produce an invalid result unless positivity is guaranteed externally.

audit_member_text: [L101-L110,L169-L178,L213-L216,L283-L286] (MED/unchecked period denominator) Frequency conversions divide by par%px or par%Trep without local validation of the required positive-period contract.
